claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations incorporating defects and oxygen impurities can accurately predict the temperature-dependent electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predictive approach is applicable in the 0–200 K regime.
The predictive approach is applicable in the 300–1200 K regime.
The approach applies to HfNbTaTiZr both without oxygen and with 1 wt.% oxygen.
The approach applies to both polycrystalline and single-crystal bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Defects and oxygen impurities affect the electrical conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
Representing defects and oxygen impurities at the atomic or mesoscale enables their effects on electrical conductivity to be accounted for.
Predicted conductivity values will be within 10% of experimental measurements across the stated temperature and oxygen-content ranges.
Experimental conductivity measurements are available for bulk HfNbTaTiZr both with and without 1 wt.% oxygen.
Predictive performance is limited by the accuracy of the molecular dynamics methodology and the quality of the experimental measurements.
A conductivity prediction for HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen at 300 K that differs from experiment by more than 15% falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines success as agreement within 10%, but the falsification rule requires an error greater than 15%. Errors above 10% and at or below 15% would violate the stated prediction without falsifying it.
